perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is Gary’s close, long-time friend; they met in middle school. Gary is a doctor.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. Gary declined, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected Gary’s overworking involved more than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything without judgment. Gary replied that it was complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan offered to help Gary prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary. He heard Gary say things were better, that he was less overwhelmed thanks to Ethan’s help, and that he had had time for a movie the previous weekend. Ethan saw Gary making efforts to change and felt hopeful and proud.
- After a year, Ethan observed Gary managing on his own and felt satisfied and happy for him. Ethan told Gary he was always a call away but believed Gary had things under control. Gary thanked him, said he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
